- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too slowly — overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., 95+ → 90+).
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in mid-to-late periods; prices often stay elevated longer than observed.
- Forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to recent low prices — underreacts to downward momentum.
- In periods with strong downward trends, model fails to adjust forecast downward quickly enough.
- Model overfits recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation even when true prices are falling.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture volatility spikes or sudden reversals.
- In low-price regimes, model tends to underestimate, especially if recent history includes a sharp drop.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to new information — true price drops are often forecasted too late or too high.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward if recent 5–7 day average is below 85% of 30d average.
- If true price drops below 80% of 30d average, forecast should be reduced by 5–10% of current value.
- If model forecast exceeds 95% of 30d average, reduce by 5–10% unless recent history shows strong upward momentum.
- If true price is below 85% of 30d average for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should be adjusted downward by 5–10%.
- Model should not forecast above 98% of 30d average unless recent history shows strong upward momentum.
- If true price is below 80% of 30d average and forecast is above 95%, reduce forecast by 10–15%.
- Model should be calibrated to respond to 3-day moving average divergence — if MA3 is falling, reduce forecast.
